sentences.text: He joined the group in November 2012 as Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer of RWE Supply and Trading GmbH, later leading that unit as its CEO, and before that spent 2005 to 2012 at Commerzbank AG in Frankfurt, including as Divisional Board Member and Head of Group Finance; earlier he worked as a management consultant at McKinsey and Company from 2000 to 2005, completed a bank traineeship at Deutsche Bank, studied economics and business administration at Duisburg and Indiana University of Pennsylvania, and earned a PhD at Humboldt University Berlin.

mgmt_bio.text: Markus Krebber, born 16 February 1973 in Kleve, Germany, has been Chief Executive Officer of RWE AG, Essen, since 1 May 2021, having served as Chief Financial Officer and Executive Board member from October 2016 to April 2021. He joined the group in November 2012 as Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer of RWE Supply and Trading GmbH, later leading that unit as its CEO, and before that spent 2005 to 2012 at Commerzbank AG in Frankfurt, including as Divisional Board Member and Head of Group Finance; earlier he worked as a management consultant at McKinsey and Company from 2000 to 2005, completed a bank traineeship at Deutsche Bank, studied economics and business administration at Duisburg and Indiana University of Pennsylvania, and earned a PhD at Humboldt University Berlin.

sentences.text: RWE's three-member Executive Board is unchanged: Krebber's contract was extended early by five years to end-June 2031, and CHRO Katja van Doren's to end-July 2029, alongside CFO Michael Mueller, appointed until 2028.

sentences.text: Below board level, Katja Wuenschel left on 31 March 2026 to join Vonovia's management board, with Sopna Sury becoming CEO of RWE Renewables Europe & Australia on 1 April 2026; Sven Utermoehlen left RWE Offshore Wind on 30 September 2026, succeeded by Tobias Keitel, with Julian Garnsey as CTO.
Krebber frames strategy around EUR 42 billion of net investment from 2026 to 2031 with unchanged return criteria, now including grids as a third pillar after raising the Amprion stake to 55%.

sentences.text: Markus Krebber, CEO since 2021, launched the "Growing Green" build-out and later scaled it back: after EUR 10bn net investment in 2024, net spending for 2025-2030 was trimmed to EUR 35bn, EUR 10bn below the original plan, with the return hurdle for new projects raised from about 8% to above 8.5%.

sentences.text: Analysts and investors read the cut and higher hurdles, alongside the running buyback, as evidence of value-oriented policy; Elliott called it a first step towards more disciplined capital allocation while criticising limited shareholder returns.
For 2025 adjusted EBITDA of EUR 5.1bn reached the upper end of guidance, with leverage at 2.1x against a self-imposed 3.0x limit.

sentences.quote: RWE's adjusted EBITDA for the current fiscal year is now expected to be between EUR 5.75 billion and EUR 6.35 billion. Adjusted net income is forecast to reach between EUR 1.95 billion and EUR 2.45 billion
sentences.text: RWE raised its 2026 guidance to adjusted EBITDA of EUR 5.75-6.35 billion after first-half adjusted EBITDA of EUR 3.0 billion and adjusted earnings per share of EUR 1.77, with adjusted net income seen at EUR 1,950-2,450 million.

Growth is underpinned by a large build-out pipeline, with 752 megawatts commissioned since the start of 2026 and a further 10.3 gigawatts under construction, supported by a EUR 42 billion investment plan to 2031.

sentences.quote: Following the increase in RWE's stake in Amprion, earnings contributions from the transmission system operator will be reported in the new "Regulated Grid Infrastructure" segment from fiscal year 2027 onwards.
sentences.text: The larger stake in transmission system operator Amprion adds regulated grid earnings and underpins the target of lifting adjusted earnings per share to EUR 4.55 in 2031.

As a result of this rigorous risk management strategy, RWE has decreased planned investment through 2030 by EUR 10 billion.
sentences.text: Capital discipline is explicit: the required return on new projects was raised to 8.5% and planned spending through 2030 cut.
Earnings are diversified across offshore wind, onshore wind and solar, flexible generation and trading, on a Baa2 issuer rating.
